display_title: Breakthroughs in Advanced Materials for Electricity Generation, Storage and Transmission – European Innovation Council (EIC)
call_module_title: Breakthroughs in Advanced Materials for Electricity Generation, Storage and Transmission
executive_summary: This EIC Pathfinder Challenge funds research projects that identify, develop and validate in the lab devices based on new advanced materials, including nanomaterials, for one of three pillars of the electricity system: energy generation, energy storage, or next-generation transmission grids with much lower losses, higher capacity and better resilience. Every project must design its innovation for grid integration and deliver a mid- to long-term roadmap for integrating it into electrical grids. Single legal entities (start-ups, SMEs, universities, research organisations, but not mid-caps or large companies), consortia of two entities from two countries, or consortia of three or more entities from three countries may apply. The grant is a Research and Innovation Action lump sum at 100% of eligible costs, with up to EUR 4 million per project considered appropriate; the EUR 82 million Challenges budget is shared roughly equally across three Challenges. The single-stage deadline is 29 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time; the call opens on 27 May 2027.
status_rationale: The Challenge funds lab-validated devices based on new advanced materials for electricity generation, storage or transmission grids with lower losses, higher capacity and better resilience, designed for grid integration (EIC Work Programme 2027, Section II.2.1, pp. 41-43). It touches TenneT's core field: it shares transmission assets and grid efficiency with SuedLink, the 2GW Program and InterOPERA, and grid resilience with the TSO Innovation Alliance, but works at TRL 2-4 rather than on deployed equipment. Large companies are excluded only from single-beneficiary projects, so TenneT TSO B.V. could be a funded beneficiary at 100% of eligible costs in a consortium (Section II.2, pp. 35-36). C1.3 fits because TenneT would most plausibly be a partner contributing grid requirements to a materials-research consortium.
